extracted.intended_audience: researchers and administrators seeking NCI research grant funding (investigators applying for NCI/NIH grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level standards for obtaining NCI research grant support, including how funding decisions are guided and where applicants can find programmatic resources and historical funding information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the best science
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for the best science underpins everything NCI does. NCI supports the best scientists and research projects through a rigorous grant application and peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative standard: scientific excellence (quality of science and investigators) is the central criterion for NCI funding decisions. Applicants should emphasize the scientific merit and potential impact of their work. No itemized review criteria are listed on this page; applicants should consult linked peer review guidance for formal review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous grant application and peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: NCI supports the best scientists and research projects through a rigorous grant application and peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that funding decisions are made via structured peer review. Applicants must prepare grant applications suitable for peer review (clear aims, rigorous approach, qualified investigators, adequate environment). Use NIH/NCI peer review materials for detailed scoring criteria and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: To fund the most promising scientific opportunities, NCI formulates guidelines based on expected allocations of funds, program requirements, and prior history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit factors that drive funding decisions: availability of funds (expected allocations), alignment with program requirements, and historical funding patterns. Applicants should be aware that even meritorious applications are funded depending on program priorities and budget realities; consult program announcements and program officers about fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of Research Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Find funding opportunities to support cancer research and training organized by type, special initiative, and research topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select funding opportunities (FOAs) that match the application type (e.g., R01, K award), any special initiatives, and the specific research topic. Properly matching the application to the correct opportunity and programmatic initiative increases alignment with program requirements and improves fundability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Grant Resources to navigate NCI and NIH processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources to help with the NCI and NIH grants and funding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to use available resources (guides, FAQs, contacts) to ensure compliance with application requirements and to prepare competitive submissions. This includes following agency-specific instructions, deadlines, and application formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Annual Reports on Extramural Activities for funding patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports from the NCI Division of Extramural Activities include historical grant referral and funding pattern information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and program staff can use historical referral and funding pattern data to understand past funding behavior, paylines, and program-level priorities. This transparency helps applicants set realistic expectations and tailor proposals to likely programmatic interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Program Contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information for program directors in NCI's Divisions, Offices, and Centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging program contacts is an expected part of preparing and positioning an application—discussing fit, appropriateness of specific FOAs, and program priorities with program directors can inform application strategy and improve alignment with program requirements.
